profiles.name: Dan94
profiles.profile: This guy is basically a one-man putting clinic with a functioning tour van attached. When the irons are cooking, the rest of the field is just out here donating strokes and pretending it’s close. The weird part is the floor is high even when the long game isn’t perfect, because the flatstick keeps dragging the corpse to the finish line. If the tee ball shows up too, everybody else is playing for second and a clean shirt.

profiles.name: MattF
profiles.profile: MattF lives in that annoying little pocket where nothing looks glamorous and yet the card somehow stays alive. The driver is not exactly out here threatening local traffic laws, but the approach game and the putter keep bailing out the mess like two emergency contractors. When the ball-striking gets sloppy, he still finds a way to keep the round on a leash instead of letting it go feral. Not flashy, just stubborn as hell about refusing to fully implode.

profiles.name: KeithK75
profiles.profile: KeithK75 is the classic guy who can hit irons like he’s trying to leave dents in the flagstick, then wander into a bunker and act surprised the round has consequences. The ball-striking is loud enough to keep him in the hunt, but the short game has had enough weird little detours to keep the whole thing from looking tidy. When the putter cooperates, he’s a problem; when it doesn’t, the card gets real wobbly in a hurry. Very much a live wire, not a smooth operation.

profiles.name: BigTime
profiles.profile: BigTime keeps trying to brute-force golf and the short game keeps filing restraining orders. There are enough flashes in the long game to make you squint and think, “okay, maybe,” and then the scoring clubs show up and kick the door off the hinges. The story here is not subtle: too many extra hits, too many three-putt-ish adventures, not enough clean escapes when the hole starts bleeding. He can survive stretches, but the round usually turns into a brawl with his own wedge play.

profiles.name: DREADFUL
profiles.profile: One round is enough to know this file comes with some ugly baggage around the greens and on the dance floor. The short game at least threw a little life raft into the water, but the putter was basically a brick with a grip, and the whole thing spent way too much time counting extra taps. That’s the kind of scorecard that makes you wonder if the hole shrank overnight. Short version: there is work to do, and a therapist for the flatstick wouldn’t hurt.

profiles.name: tnboles77
profiles.profile: tnboles77 is living in the land of small-ball suffering: not enough tee-ball pop, not enough greens, and way too much time asking the putter to do CPR. There was one round where the card finally opened up and the short game showed a pulse, which is promising, but the rest of the window is still pretty damn muddy. This profile says “grind” more than “ceiling.” If the driver and approach ever decide to join the same meeting, there’s something here.
